paper_metadata.title: Capturing dynamics with noisy quantum computers

experiments.description: Numerical regression experiment training a parameterized quantum circuit to approximate the linear function f*(x)=x/(2π) on different input normalizations using the L2 loss.

algorithm.variant: parameterized quantum circuit regression with generalized trigonometric series
algorithm.ansatz: 3-layer circuit with alternating Rx data-encoding and Ry trainable rotations; each qubit measured in the Pauli-Z basis

problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize empirical L2 regression loss between PQC output f_theta(x) and target function f*(x)=x/(2π)

problem_instance.description: One-dimensional function approximation/regression task for a linear target function on a bounded interval.

dataset_specification.description: Target function f*(x)=x/(2π), x∈[-π, π]. Training inputs were uniformly distributed along the domain; three different input normalizations were tested.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Min-max feature scaling / normalization of inputs to specified intervals.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Aggregate results over 100 repeated runs and report 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles.

experiments.description: Numerical regression experiment comparing L2 loss versus H1 loss for the same PQC regression task under two input normalizations.

algorithm.variant: parameterized quantum circuit regression with Sobolev H1 loss
algorithm.ansatz: 3-layer circuit with alternating Rx data-encoding and Ry trainable rotations; each qubit measured in the Pauli-Z basis

problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the discretized Sobolev H1 loss combining function-value error and first-derivative error

problem_instance.description: One-dimensional function approximation/regression task for the linear target function f*(x)=x/(2π), evaluated with and without derivative supervision.

dataset_specification.description: Target function f*(x)=x/(2π), x∈[-π, π]. Training inputs were uniformly distributed. Two normalizations were tested: [-π/2, π/2] and [-π, π]. Derivative values were included for the H1 loss.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Min-max feature scaling / normalization of inputs to specified intervals.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Aggregate results over 100 repeated runs and compare performance under H1 vs L2 loss.
